L05 | Judgment remains in deciding which facts are important enough to test and what test would actually confirm them.
L06 | Judgment remains in recognizing when a code or hash is long or critical enough to require programmatic copying and in confirming the copy is exact.
L07 | Judgment remains in knowing when a written time must be read from a clock and which clock source or time convention to use.
L08 | Judgment remains in determining whether an empty or short result reflects a real absence or only a limited or failed search.
L09 | Judgment remains in deciding what observable outcome would prove the operation actually succeeded and how deeply to inspect it.
L10 | Judgment remains in deciding which additional sources or locations could change the answer enough to be worth checking.
L11 | Judgment remains in distinguishing a wrong location or reading from true loss before declaring something lost.
L12 | Judgment remains in deciding when a quotation is exact enough and when evidence is sufficient to name a real cause.
L13 | Judgment remains in choosing a different reviewer whose perspective is likely to catch the specific error in the work.
L14 | Judgment remains in determining what observable behavior would demonstrate that a saved change or setting is actually in effect.
L15 | Judgment remains in discerning what the person is actually asking for and resisting the urge to add something else.
L16 | Judgment remains in determining whether an external check is genuinely independent and sufficient before marking an answer checked.
L17 | Judgment remains in identifying the single check that would actually decide whether the work is done or verified.
